strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Lifecycle pricing of the turboprop and turbofan aftermarket: spare parts, labour rates and end-of-life engine governance.
posting_evidence: Senior Manager, Longueuil, in-office five days; posted 2026-10-08 (Built In copy of a bilingual posting).
Builds lifecycle pricing strategies for new, mid-life and end-of-life engines and leads in-service strategy for engine programs.
Assesses the impact of proposed spare-parts and labour-rate increases and helps define a discount and pricing-concession strategy.
Feeds a commercial strategy dashboard used by P&WC's Executive Committee; leads 'Project Vitamin E' (end-of-life engine governance).
Reporting line inconsistent: Associate Director (English) vs Manager (French), Pricing & Lifecycle Strategy.

news.summary: IATA welcomed P&WC contract changes, made after a European Commission competition probe, that lift restrictions on network maintenance shops so independent suppliers can access used PT6 and PW100-series parts and services.

strategy_updates.interpretation: P&WC appears to be professionalizing aftermarket pricing across the full engine lifecycle, where spare parts and shop labour carry most of the margin. Inference: the September 2026 loosening of used-parts restrictions under EU competition pressure raises competition from used and independent material, which makes disciplined list-price increases, concession rules and end-of-life governance more important now. The role is an execution-heavy senior manager seat with direct line of sight to the Executive Committee, not the head of pricing.
open_questions: How will the used-parts contract changes affect price increase plans and concession policy for PT6 and PW100 parts?
What decision rights does this role have over annual list-price increases versus the Associate Director?
What is 'Project Vitamin E' expected to deliver, and on what timeline?
strategy_updates.caveat: Read from a Built In copy; the employer posting could not be opened, and no P&WC price-list data was found.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Centralizing and governing pricing after acquisitions while pushing repeated list-price increases through the channel.
strategy_updates.current_model: Quote-based pricing sold through partners and MSPs; hardware appliances plus term subscriptions (per reseller notices).
posting_evidence: Senior Director, remote Canada, base CAD 184,000–306,000 plus bonus; parallel UK posting on Lever.
Mandate: build a centralized Pricing Operations function covering strategy, analytics and deal support for SecOps.
Replace episodic reviews with a segment-aware pricing cadence; set up a pricing council and governance with advance communication to sales and finance.
Direct AI-assisted monitoring of competitor pricing, discounting and discount depth; metrics include decision-to-communication time and discount discipline.
Strong dotted line to the Network Security group to keep pricing aligned across both businesses.

news.summary: Citing a 1 September Sophos partner email, a reseller reported a further 10% increase on XGS hardware and hardware-bound subscriptions plus AP6 access points, a 7.5% rise for Sophos Email, and AP6 support up from 5% to 10% of hardware price; effective 1 November 2026 for term licences and 1 January 2027 for MSP, after a 10% XGS increase on 1 July 2026.

strategy_updates.interpretation: Sophos looks to be moving pricing from ad hoc, product-by-product decisions to a governed central function, likely to manage price realization across a portfolio that has grown through acquisitions. Inference: two 10% hardware increases within four months suggest margin pressure and a need for better discount control and communication to partners, which this role is explicitly asked to build. Expect a hands-on build mandate: new team, cadence and AI tooling, with heavy channel and sales change management.
open_questions: Who does the role report to, and does it own price-setting decisions or only the process and analytics?
How is pricing split between SecOps and Network Security today, and who arbitrates conflicts?
How have partners and MSPs responded to the 2026 increases (discount pressure, churn)?
strategy_updates.caveat: Price-increase details come from a reseller blog, not a Sophos release; Sophos does not publish list prices.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Shifting from per-seat tiers to a hybrid seat-plus-consumption model built around GitLab Credits and the new Flex commitment.
strategy_updates.current_model: Per-user subscription tiers (Free, Premium, Ultimate) plus usage-based GitLab Credits for Duo Agent Platform; GitLab Flex combines seats, credits and new capabilities in one annual commitment; Secrets Manager sold as a usage-based add-on for Premium and Ultimate on GitLab.com.
posting_evidence: Two concurrent senior IC openings, both Remote Canada or US: Lead Pricing Strategist and Staff Commercial Pricing Strategist (US base USD 139,200–235,200; no Canada range).
Lead role: pricing and packaging across Premium, Ultimate, GitLab Duo and AI/usage-based products, SKU mapping for launches and post-launch monitoring.
Staff role: enterprise agreements, bundling, channel and cloud-marketplace pricing, discount frameworks and competitive deal programs.
Both expect influence over VP/SVP stakeholders without authority and documentation of pricing decisions in the public handbook; staff role asks for hands-on work with production AI agents.

news.summary: GitLab reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $286.3M (+21% YoY), introduced GitLab Flex (one annual commitment covering seats, GitLab Credits and new capabilities with adjustable monthly reservations) and launched Secrets Manager as a usage-based add-on.

strategy_updates.interpretation: GitLab is trying to monetize AI agents through consumption without disrupting its seat-based core, and Flex is the bridge that lets enterprise buyers commit once and shift spend between seats and credits. Inference: hiring both a product-pricing lead and an enterprise/channel pricing specialist at the same time suggests the packaging is set and the work now is making it sell through enterprise deals, marketplaces and partners. Candidates should expect usage-metering, credit pricing and discount governance to be core.
open_questions: How are credit consumption and Flex reservations priced and discounted in enterprise deals?
Who owns the overall pricing roadmap above these two IC roles?
What metrics define success for Duo Agent Platform monetization (credit attach, overage, net ARR)?
strategy_updates.caveat: Current model drawn from GitLab's earnings release and posting text; the public pricing page was not read today.
